scope: read-only biological tuning evidence; no stimulation/current

supported_claims.claim: SNpp39 and SNpp41 are leg proprioceptive FeCO-related systematic sensory types, with curated/public evidence placing them in hook-related chordotonal populations.
Drosophila FeCO hook neurons encode directional tibia movement, with distinct flexion-encoding and extension-encoding hook populations.
Male VNC connectome analysis predicts SNpp39 and SNpp41 exert opposing effects on tibia flexor/extensor motor circuits, consistent with distinct directionally tuned hook pathways.

annotation_conflicts.observation: Public VFB/MANC examples include a FeCO club annotation while MaleCNS and BANC examples classify SNpp39 as femoral chordotonal hook; therefore legacy/cross-dataset subtype labels are not treated as a polarity crosswalk.

Public VFB/MANC examples include claw/hook labeling differences, while BANC examples classify SNpp41 as femoral chordotonal hook; therefore subtype identity must be handled conservatively across datasets.

unresolved_claims.reason: Available reviewed/public text inspected here does not provide an explicit experimentally validated systematic-type-to-direction crosswalk. Opposing motor-circuit predictions are insufficient to assign sensory polarity by reflex inference alone.
